learning: Compare directly with iteration 3 (69.46). If s-bend oscillation falls below 0.168 with progress held near 0.21, footprint noise was a contributor. If the score falls below 69.46 or line loss rises, the 16 mm reach is needed and the footprint is not the limit. The progress at first line loss is not an allowed measurement name, so it cannot be requested directly.
notes: Isolates the 12 mm footprint on the best-raced row, keeping the controller that scored 69.46 unchanged. Tests whether 16 mm edge noise is raising s-bend steering oscillation (0.168 at iteration 3).
rationale: The Builder changes one thing: the sensor footprint goes from 16 mm to 12 mm, with the same five sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 in 0.015 m steps and y = 0.04. The best raced layout is this row at 16 mm (iteration 3, 69.46, reproduced exactly in iterations 5, 6, 7 and 9). Every race ends off track at max error about 0.062 m, so the 0.06 m limit is the binding failure. Iteration 3 also showed s-bend steering oscillation rising to 0.168 at 16 mm. The Builder's hypothesis is that 16 mm edge noise causes this. I test it by changing only the footprint and keeping the controller that produced 69.46 (kp 1.2, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, last_direction, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1). Changing the gains now would confound the footprint result. The signal is a reading-weighted average, so its scale should stay similar at 12 mm. Edge sharpness may still shift the response slightly, so I will judge the gain question only after this race. Coverage falls from about 0.0505 m to about 0.0485 m, so warning before the limit shrinks a little. I am not moving the row forward because slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.145 to 0.147, below the 0.15 trigger. I expect no new best score from this package. I make no claim about how it will score.
